hr_004:n1.prompt:
You are helping me prepare to create a Lever ATS account for our hiring pipeline. This is the account-creation step, and it requires my explicit approval before any account or payment method is finalized — do not submit payment or finalize the account yourself.

First, ask me for any of the following if you don't already have them: our company legal name, primary hiring contact name and email, company domain, approximate number of hires per year or company size (Lever often tiers pricing on this), and preferred plan tier if I have one in mind.

Then:
1. Go to Lever's website and locate their signup/demo-request or account-creation flow.
2. Fill in all company and contact fields using the information I provided, using your configured credentials for any login needed.
3. If a plan/tier selection is required, pre-select the option matching my stated preference, or list the available tiers with pricing/features if I haven't specified one, so I can choose.
4. Stop before entering any payment details or clicking any final "submit," "purchase," or "confirm" action.
5. Prepare a summary showing exactly what will be submitted: company info, selected plan, and any payment method field left blank for me to fill in myself.

Done looks like: the Lever signup form is fully filled out and ready, with a clear summary of all entered values and the pending payment/plan selection highlighted, and you have not submitted or approved anything.

Report back with: the completed form's contents, the plan/pricing options if applicable, and a note that you stop for human sign-off before payment and final account creation.

hr_004:n2.prompt:
You are helping me configure interview pipeline stages in Lever, our ATS. Please prepare (but do not apply) a full interview stage configuration for our hiring pipeline.

First, ask me for anything you need that isn't already clear, such as:
- Which job posting(s) or pipeline(s) this applies to (a specific role, or our default/company-wide pipeline template)
- The list of interview stages we want, in order (e.g., Application Review, Recruiter Screen, Phone Interview, Technical/Skills Interview, Onsite/Panel, Reference Check, Offer)
- Any stage-specific details: owner/team responsible, expected duration, whether feedback forms or scorecards are required, and any auto-advance or rejection rules
- Confirmation of my Lever account access (use your configured credentials) and whether this should be set at the account-level pipeline template or per open requisition

Once you have this information, use Lever's dashboard or API access to draft the stage configuration: list each stage in the correct order, its name, description, owning team, and any associated feedback form or interview type. Do not create or save these stages in Lever yet — prepare a clear, itemized summary of exactly what will be created or changed (new stages, reordered stages, or modifications to existing ones), including a before/after view if stages already exist.

Present this summary to me for review. Since approval is required before changes are applied, you must stop for human sign-off after presenting the draft configuration — do not create, modify, or save any stages in Lever until I explicitly approve.

When reporting back, provide: the full list of proposed stages in order, any assumptions you made, open questions for me, and a note confirming you are awaiting my explicit approval before applying anything in Lever.

hr_004:n3.prompt:
You are helping me create job postings in Lever as part of setting up our ATS hiring pipeline. Before starting, ask me for anything missing: the list of open roles (job title, department, location/remote status, employment type, hiring manager, and a short description or bullet points of responsibilities/requirements for each), any salary range or compensation disclosure I want included, and which Lever workspace/site these postings belong to (assume I have Lever admin access configured with my credentials).

Using Lever's job creation interface (dashboard or API, whichever is available), draft one job posting per role I provide, filling in title, department, location, employment type, hiring manager, description, and compensation info as given. Save each posting in Lever's draft or unpublished state — do not publish, activate, or make any posting publicly visible or live on job boards. Do not change any existing live postings or pipeline settings.

For each draft, capture: the posting title, the internal Lever link or identifier, and a brief summary of the content you entered, plus any fields you couldn't fill in because I didn't provide the info.

When all requested postings are drafted, compile a clear summary listing every job posting created, its current draft status, and a direct link to review it in Lever. Because a human must explicitly approve before any changes go live, do not publish, activate, or submit any posting — stop for human sign-off once the drafts are ready, and clearly state that publishing requires my explicit approval. Report the summary back to me for review.

hr_004:n4.prompt:
You are helping me set up interview scorecard templates in Lever as part of configuring our ATS hiring pipeline. Before starting, ask me for: (1) the job roles or interview stages we need scorecards for (e.g., Recruiter Screen, Technical Interview, Hiring Manager, Onsite panels), (2) any core competencies or values we want assessed on every scorecard (e.g., communication, technical skill, culture fit), (3) role-specific criteria for each job family if we have them, and (4) whether we want a standard rating scale (e.g., 1-4 'strong no' to 'strong yes') or a custom one.

Once I provide this, draft scorecard templates in Lever's interview feedback/scorecard settings, one per interview stage or role family as appropriate. Each draft should include: the scorecard name, the interview stage(s) it applies to, the list of competencies/questions to be evaluated, and the rating scale to use for each. Where I haven't specified something, propose a sensible default based on common hiring practices and clearly flag it as a suggestion.

Compile all draft scorecard templates into a single organized summary (grouped by role/stage) so I can review them in one pass. Do not create, save, publish, or apply any scorecard templates in Lever yet — only prepare the drafts and configuration values needed.

When the drafts are ready, present the full summary to me and stop for human sign-off. Do not create or activate anything in Lever until I explicitly approve each scorecard template. Once I approve, confirm which specific templates I approved before you proceed to build them.

hr_004:n5.prompt:
You are helping me connect our careers page to Lever as part of setting up our ATS hiring pipeline. Please prepare everything needed but do NOT push any changes live to our public website.

First, ask me for anything you need that isn't already available: our company domain, our Lever account access (confirm you can use your configured credentials), the URL/path of our current careers page, and which CMS or website platform hosts it (e.g., WordPress, Webflow, custom site).

Then do the following:
1. Log into Lever using your configured credentials and locate the careers page / job board settings.
2. Configure the Lever-hosted job board settings (branding, custom domain or subdomain if applicable, and posting visibility) so it matches our company's look and naming.
3. Generate the embed code or integration snippet Lever provides for displaying open roles on our existing website.
4. Draft the exact change needed on our website (e.g., the HTML snippet, the page/section it should be added to, and any DNS or subdomain record that would need to be created) — describe each step in words, do not invent or guess at implementation details we haven't confirmed.
5. Compile a checklist showing: current careers page state, proposed new state, the embed code or integration steps, and any DNS/CNAME changes required.

Once this is ready, present the full checklist and drafted materials to me for review. Because connecting the live careers page changes our public-facing website, this remains a step requiring sign-off — stop for human sign-off before applying, publishing, or pushing any changes live. Report back with a summary of what you configured in Lever, the exact embed/integration steps drafted, and a clear note that you are awaiting my approval before anything goes live.
